key_insight: CiteGuard-RAG shows that getting evidence back is not enough—AI answers also need runtime validation to stay grounded, cite correctly, and refuse when support is weak. The paper combines retrieval, citation constraints, and grounding checks to make RAG more trustworthy.
problem_solved: It addresses the gap between evidence retrieval and reliable answering: RAG systems may still produce unsupported, uncited, or overconfident responses even when relevant documents are found.
method: Uses hybrid semantic + lexical retrieval to improve evidence search quality.
Generates answers under citation constraints so claims are tied to source evidence.
Applies sentence-level grounding validation at runtime and triggers single-pass regeneration when support is insufficient.
impact: This matters for practitioners building enterprise, legal, medical, or research assistants where citation accuracy and refusal behavior are critical. It offers a practical framework for making RAG outputs more auditable and trustworthy.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing retrieval -> citation-constrained generation -> grounding validation -> regeneration/refusal
Side-by-side example of grounded vs. ungrounded answers with citations highlighted
Validation checkpoint icons showing pass/fail at the sentence level
Flowchart of decision paths: answer, regenerate, or refuse
paper_title: CiteGuard-RAG: A Validation-Centered AI System for Evidence-Grounded Question Answering
paper_authors: Sumit Barua, Guan Hong, Halil Dursunoglu, Charles Rodgers, Alvis Fong
